newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia graduate salaries diminishing - study.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia graduate salaries diminishing - study.

text.p: Starting salaries for Australia's graduates were diminishing as more students with tertiary qualifications entered the workforce, a survey found.

A graduate starting salaries survey, conducted by the Graduate Careers Council of Australia, found starting wages had fallen to 79.6 percent of average weekly earnings in 1995 from 100 percent in 1977.

"It is self evident that the advantage gained in the labour market through the completion of tertiary study has become smaller as the number of similarly qualified job seekers increase," the National Union of Students said in a statement.
As the number of people in higher education rose to 620,000 in 1995 from nearly 300,000 in 1977, the level of competitive advantage declined, the union said.
The survey found it was the lowest level of graduate starting salaries since the survey began in 1977, it said.
